fixes.explanation: Seventy years is what Daniel understood from the sacred books. It was the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet, and it was about the desolation of Jerusalem (Daniel 9:2). Daniel read that number and it landed. I've been stuck in the back of a junk drawer for a long stretch myself, so I know a number like that means something when you're counting.

Daniel turns to the Lord God to seek Him "…by prayer and petition, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes." (Daniel 9:3) Sackcloth is rough cloth, the opposite of your comfiest sweater. I think a man dressed like that means business. I bet he isn't treating this prayer as a quick stop on his way somewhere else.

Gold, silver and incense are fancy things, but this verse doesn't list any of them. It says Daniel turns to the Lord God by prayer and petition, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes (Daniel 9:3). No gift basket in the list, no shiny extras. Fasting, sackcloth and ashes is what the verse names.

Prophets is it. Daniel confesses that they did not listen to God's servants the prophets, who spoke in His name to their kings, leaders, fathers, and all the people of the land (Daniel 9:6). Those messengers went from the top of the ladder all the way down. And Daniel owns it with a plain "we."

Judges aren't named in this verse, friend. Daniel says the servants of God they didn't listen to were the prophets (Daniel 9:6). Those prophets spoke in His name to the kings, the leaders, the fathers, and all the people of the land. That's a whole lot of ears that should've been open, so the blank wants prophets.

Silence and distance is the opposite of what Daniel says. He says compassion and forgiveness belong to the Lord our God, even though they rebelled against Him (Daniel 9:9). Those two words don't sound like a locked door to me. I think a man who says them to God is talking to Someone he expects to listen.

Strength and secrecy aren't what Daniel names in this verse. He says compassion and forgiveness belong to the Lord our God, even though the people rebelled against Him (Daniel 9:9). Those are the two words he picks for God here. Secrecy never comes up.

Moab, another nation named in the Bible, isn't in this verse. Daniel says God brought His people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand (Daniel 9:15). That's the act he lifts up as he prays, like pulling out the one photo that says it all. Egypt fills the blank.

A sword and a shield aren't what Gabriel says he came with. He says, "O Daniel, I have come now to give you insight and understanding." (Daniel 9:22) Gear isn't part of what he says he brings. Understanding is.

Careful, baker, this one's a sneaky one! Gabriel does say it. The seventy weeks are decreed "…to bring in everlasting righteousness…" (Daniel 9:24). It sits right there in the list with ending sin and making atonement for iniquity. So the answer is True.
